actor: Parameter-selection lead, HAWK submission design team
job: Re-deriving HAWK's concrete security estimates under the published lattice symmetry and re-sizing the parameter sets that carry the claimed levels.
outcome: A revised HAWK specification with enlarged HAWK-512 and HAWK-1024 parameter sets and re-computed gate-count tables restoring the claimed security levels.
motivation: Enlarging parameters costs key and signature size but concedes nothing about how the symmetry was found; a rebuttal would cost the submission's credibility.

task.who: HAWK design team's parameter-selection and security-estimate subgroup
task.what: Re-size HAWK-512 and HAWK-1024 parameter sets
task.where: The HAWK specification and its security-analysis chapter
task.why: Published parameters must support the level they claim
task.how: Lattice-estimator gate-count recomputation against the disclosed symmetry

actor: Standardisation process manager, NIST post-quantum signature programme
job: Routing the published cryptanalysis onto the official comment record and asking the HAWK team for an on-record response before the round closes.
outcome: A NIST-process posting carrying the HAWK team's answer, the enlarged parameter sets, into the standardisation round's public record.
motivation: A round report cannot advance a candidate whose published gate counts no longer match the security level it was selected against.

task.who: NIST post-quantum standardisation staff and official-comment moderators
task.what: Post the cryptanalysis and solicit the team's response
task.where: The pqc-forum mailing list and official comments page
task.why: The round record needs the design team on record
task.how: Official-comment thread plus round status-report drafting

actor: Lattice cryptanalysis group at an academic or industrial security lab
job: Rerunning the HAWK-256 key recovery end to end to settle whether the claimed 2^38 work factor holds outside the publishing lab.
outcome: An independent reproduction of the roughly three-hour key recovery, closing the gap a rebuttal would otherwise have room to exploit.
motivation: Settling this claim costs one afternoon of rented compute, cheap enough that being first to check is worth more than waiting.

task.who: Academic lattice cryptanalysis group with a cloud compute budget
task.what: Reproduce the 2^38 HAWK-256 challenge key recovery
task.where: Rented 96-core servers, written up as a preprint
task.why: An outside run removes the option of disputing the symmetry
task.how: Rented 96-core server run against the challenge parameter set

job: Re-tuning and re-benchmarking the reference code at the enlarged parameters, then regenerating the key, signature and known-answer test vectors.
outcome: An implementation and test-vector set matching the revised specification, so enlarged parameters ship as a usable submission rather than a table.
motivation: The scheme's selling point is compact signatures, so the team must show what the enlargement actually costs before reviewers accept it.

task.what: Re-benchmark key and signature sizes at enlarged parameters
task.where: The HAWK reference codebase and known-answer test vectors
task.why: A specification revision ships only with matching implementation numbers
task.how: SUPERCOP-style benchmarking and regenerated known-answer test vectors

actor: Responsible-disclosure lead, frontier-lab red team publishing the cryptanalysis
job: Putting the challenge instance, its parameters and the verification path on record so third parties can settle the key-recovery claim unaided.
outcome: A checkable artifact, challenge parameters plus verification steps, that makes reproducing the result cheaper than arguing about whether it holds.
motivation: A result nobody can rerun stays a press claim; the lab's case for model-assisted cryptanalysis depends on outsiders confirming the numbers.

task.who: Frontier-lab red team and responsible-disclosure coordinators
task.what: Publish the challenge instance and verification steps
task.where: The lab's research write-up and accompanying artifact release
task.why: Reproducibility is what makes conceding cheaper than contesting
task.how: Coordinated disclosure to the design team plus public artifacts

job: Encoding the halving symmetry into the public cost model so any re-sized HAWK parameters are computed against a corrected estimate.
outcome: A patched estimator whose gate-count output reflects the symmetry, giving the revised parameter sets a cost model reviewers already trust.
motivation: Every lattice submission sizes its parameters against this tooling, so an estimator blind to the symmetry hands out numbers nobody can defend.

task.who: Lattice estimator maintainers and contributing cryptanalysts
task.what: Encode the halving symmetry into the public cost model
task.where: The open lattice-estimator repository and its regression suite
task.why: Re-sized parameters need a cost model carrying the symmetry
task.how: Cost-model patch with regression tests over known parameter sets
